handoff.purpose: run_gate: advisory regression ratchet comparing current tier-1 results to a stored baseline.

symbols.name: run_gate
symbols.note: Runs tier-1 eval, compares per-task recall to baseline, returns a dict with regression/improvement/new/missing/errored/focus-withheld lists and a passed flag.

claims.text: ADVISORY regression ratchet. Replays ``tasks`` (default TASKS) against a stored baseline.json and flags any PRIMARY-tier task whose recall DECREASED.
claims.why: The loop compares cur_recall < base_recall for primary-tier tasks and adds to regressions; non-primary tasks are skipped via continue.

claims.text: Compares PER TASK, never on a mean
claims.why: The code iterates per-task and compares individual recall values; no aggregation is performed.

claims.text: Workflow before shipping a slice-heuristic change: python -m daedalus.eval --gate
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the CLI entry point or argument parsing; cannot verify the command line flag.

claims.text: Expect PASS. A FAIL means either a real regression (fix the slicer) or an intentional, reviewed label change
claims.why: The gate returns a 'passed' boolean; the meaning of FAIL and the prescribed actions are not enforced in this code.

claims.text: update the baseline EXPLICITLY (never automatically): python -m daedalus.eval --update-baseline
claims.why: No baseline-writing logic appears in this chunk; the CLI flag is not present here.

claims.text: GUARDRAIL: this gate is ADVISORY ONLY. It is a local developer command plus a unit test (there is no CI in this repo -- verified: no .github/workflows). It must never be wired to block an autonomous action.
claims.why: The 'advisory' flag is set to True, but the absence of CI and the prohibition on blocking autonomous actions cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (see ``run_tier1``) have no recall to compare and are SPLIT by tier, not folded into ``regressions``
claims.why: When 'error' in t, the task is appended to errored_primary or errored_quarantine and continue skips the regression check.

claims.text: PRIMARY tier -- FAILS the gate loudly (``errored_primary``, named in the rendered report).
claims.why: errored_primary is included in the result and contributes to the 'passed' condition (len(errored_primary) == 0).

claims.text: QUARANTINE tier -- reported only (``errored_quarantine``), never fails the gate
claims.why: errored_quarantine is returned but not part of the 'passed' condition.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- lane A1) are likewise SPLIT OUT, not folded into ``regressions``
claims.why: If t.get('focus_withheld') is truthy, the task is appended to focus_withheld and continue skips the regression check.

claims.text: a task that TRANSITIONS to focus-withheld this run has no ``recall`` to compare (fail-closed is not "recall dropped to 0")
claims.why: The code checks focus_withheld before comparing recall, so no comparison occurs for such tasks.

claims.text: Reported in its own ``focus_withheld`` section, regardless of tier, and never fails the gate.
claims.why: focus_withheld is returned as a separate list and is not part of the 'passed' condition; the code does not check tier for focus_withheld.

claims.text: quarantine is never gated, see module docstring
claims.why: The line 'if not _is_primary_tier(t['label_tier']): continue' skips all non-primary tasks, including quarantine.

observations.what: The `passed` flag does not consider `missing_tasks` or `new_tasks`; a task that disappears from baseline or appears new does not fail the gate.
The `advisory` flag is hardcoded to True, but the docstring says it must never block autonomous actions; this is a policy statement not enforceable here.
The code assumes `baseline_tasks.get(t['id'])` returns a dict with 'recall' key; if the baseline format changes, this could raise KeyError, but no error handling is present.
The `focus_withheld` check uses `t.get('focus_withheld')` which is truthy for any non-empty value, not just boolean True; this might categorize tasks with a non-empty string as focus-withheld.

risks: line 917 | medium | The gate passes even if tasks are missing from baseline or new tasks appear, which may hide drift in the task set. | Check whether missing_tasks or new_tasks should affect 'passed'.
